title: Quick check: Screen Readers and Accessible Names

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Screen Readers and Accessible Names”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Accessible labels should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Accessible labels should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Screen Readers and Accessible Names: Accessible labels should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Accessible labels?
options: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Screen Readers and Accessible Names: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Screen Readers and Accessible Names” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Screen Readers and Accessible Names: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
